headline: Sensex and Nifty trade lower amid heavy FII selling despite record GST collections and manufacturing PMI recovery

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) accelerated selling with $2 billion outflows over the last two days
The benchmark indices are on track for their eighth consecutive weekly decline
Auto and cement sectors are acting as the primary drags on the market today
A significant hike in Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) prices to ₹137 per litre is impacting aviation sentiment
whatHappening: Gross GST collections in September rose 14.7% year-on-year to approximately ₹2.04 lakh crore
Manufacturing PMI showed recovery in September driven by increased output and job growth
MTNL shares witnessed a sharp surge of over 17% despite the broader market decline
Major auto companies including Eicher Motors and M&M reported positive sales growth for September
summary: The Indian stock market opened lower on October 1, with the Sensex and Nifty pressured by sustained FII selling and sectoral weakness in autos and cement. Despite the downturn, macroeconomic data remained robust as GST collections hit record highs and manufacturing PMI indicated a recovery in output. Individual stocks like MTNL saw significant gains, while auto majors reported healthy sales growth even as their share prices dragged.
